units.source_text: 连忙岔开话头，继续言道：

en.t: He quickly changed the subject and went on to say:

units.source_text: “自今以后，我总想永不再做疚心之事，静掩禅关，专心修持，为来世积福。

en.t: From now on, I wish never again to do anything that burdens my conscience, but to close myself quietly behind the gate of religious practice, devote myself to discipline, and store up blessings for the next life.

units.source_text: 只是回思过去，我毫无勋业值得一生怀念，不免遗憾耳。

en.t: Yet when I look back on the past, I have no great achievement worth remembering for a lifetime, and I cannot help feeling regret.

units.source_text: 惟膝下有小女一人，现仅四岁，成长之日尚远。

en.t: I have only one little daughter at my knee; she is now just four years old, and the day when she will be grown is still far off.

units.source_text: 我今不揣冒昧，欲以此女奉托，指望靠她光大门第。

en.t: Though I know it is presumptuous, I now wish to entrust this girl to you, hoping that through her our house may be brought to greater honor.

units.source_text: 我死之后，务请多多栽培。”

en.t: After I am dead, I beg you to give her every care and guidance.

units.source_text: 梅壶女御态度异常文雅，只是隐隐约约地回答了一言两语。

en.t: The Umetsubo Consort behaved with extraordinary refinement and answered only vaguely, with a word or two.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣听了觉得十分可亲，便静静地坐在那里，直到日暮。

en.t: Hearing this, Genji, the Inner Minister, found her very dear, and he sat there quietly until dusk.

units.source_text: 又继续言道：

en.t: Then he continued:

units.source_text: “光大门第之望，姑且不谈。

en.t: Let us set aside, for the moment, any hopes of raising the honor of the house.

units.source_text: 目前我所企望的，一年四时流转之中，春花秋叶，风雨晦明，应有赏心悦目之景。

en.t: What I hope for now is that, as the four seasons pass through the year, the spring flowers and autumn leaves, the wind and rain, the clear days and dark days, will all offer scenes that delight the heart and eye.

units.source_text: 春日林花烂漫，秋天郊野绮丽，孰优孰劣，古人各持一说，争论已久。

en.t: In spring the woodland flowers bloom in profusion, and in autumn the fields are splendid; as to which is better, people of old held different views and debated it for ages.

units.source_text: 毕竟何者最可赏心悦目，未有定论。

en.t: In the end, there is still no settled judgment on which most delights the heart and eye.

units.source_text: 在中国，诗人都说春花如锦，其美无比；

en.t: In China, poets all say that spring flowers are like brocade and that their beauty is beyond compare;

units.source_text: 而在日本的和歌中，则又谓‘春天只见群花放，不及清秋逸兴长’。

en.t: but in Japanese waka, it is also said that spring merely shows countless flowers in bloom and cannot match the lasting pleasure of clear autumn.

units.source_text: 我等面对四时景色，但觉神移目眩。

en.t: When we face the scenery of the four seasons, our spirits are simply carried away and our eyes dazzled.

units.source_text: 至于花色鸟声，孰优孰劣，实难分辨。

en.t: As for the colors of flowers and the songs of birds, it is truly hard to tell which is superior and which inferior.

units.source_text: 我想在这狭小的庭院内，广栽春花，移植秋草，并养些不知名的鸣虫，以点缀四时景色，供你等欣赏。

en.t: I would like to plant many spring flowers in this small garden, transplant autumn grasses, and keep some nameless singing insects, so as to adorn the scenery of the four seasons for all of you to enjoy.

units.source_text: 但不知你对于春和秋，喜爱哪一季节？”

en.t: But I wonder, between spring and autumn, which season do you prefer?

units.source_text: 梅壶女御觉得难于奉复。

en.t: The Umetsubo Consort found it difficult to answer.

units.source_text: 但闭口不答，又觉太不知趣，只得勉强答道：

en.t: Yet to remain silent seemed far too tactless, so she could only force herself to reply:

units.source_text: “此事古人都难于判别，何况我等。

en.t: This is something even people of old found hard to judge, so how much more so for people like us.

units.source_text: 诚如尊见：四时景色，皆有可观。

en.t: It is exactly as you say: the scenery of all four seasons has something worth admiring.

units.source_text: 但昔人有云：‘秋夜相思特地深’；

en.t: But someone long ago said, 'On autumn nights, longing is especially deep';

units.source_text: 我每当秋夜，便思念如朝露般消失的我母，故我觉得秋天更为可爱。”

en.t: whenever an autumn night comes, I think of my mother, who vanished like morning dew, and so autumn seems still dearer to me.

units.source_text: 这话似乎没有多少理由，信口道来，但源氏内大臣觉得非常可爱。

en.t: The words seemed to have little reasoning behind them and to have been spoken offhand, but Genji, the Inner Minister, found them extremely charming.

units.source_text: 他情不自禁，赠诗一绝：

en.t: Unable to restrain his feelings, he offered her a poem:
